stem:
Anvi has the fraction $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of a roti. She wants another fraction for the same quantity of that roti.

Which plan gives an equivalent fraction?

options.text: Change only the numerator to $6$ and keep the denominator $4$.
Write $\dfrac{6}{8}$ even when the new pair is no longer about the same roti.
Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number, for example write $\dfrac{6}{8}$.
First convert $\dfrac{3}{4}$ into a decimal; equivalence requires that conversion.

teacher.key_rationale: Equivalent fractions keep the same quantity by scaling numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor. A changes only one part. B drops the same-quantity condition. D adds an unnecessary decimal step.
